info.title: Cbox ID API
info.description:
Every Cbox ID management plane on one host: `https://api.cboxid.com/v1`.

**The credential decides where a request acts, never the host.**

- An environment key (`Bearer cbid_env_…`) acts in the environment it was minted in.
- An access token acts in the environment that issued it (`iss`). A token for the platform root acts for its person: the organization they are on, their own account (`/v1/me`), and — for an operator — the deployment (`/v1/admin`). To act inside one environment of the organization, name it in `Cbox-Environment` (its id or slug).
- An organization key (`Bearer cbid_org_…`) acts on its organization: `/v1/organization`, `/v1/projects`, `/v1/environments`, `/v1/members`, `/v1/invitations`, `/v1/organization-keys`.

A token is accepted for the audience `https://api.cboxid.com` or `https://app.cboxid.com/mcp`, and, during the transition, an issuer's own `{issuer}/mcp`.

**Shapes.** A resource is the object itself, with `object` naming what it is. A list is `{"object": "list", "data": […], "has_more": …, "next_cursor": …}`; pass `next_cursor` as `after` for the next page. A failure is an RFC 9457 problem (`application/problem+json`) whose `error` is a stable code and whose `type` links to its explanation; a validation failure adds `errors`, keyed by field. An action that needs a person's approval answers `202` with the approval it waits for (`object: "approval"`) and its `poll_url`.

**A child is addressed directly.** `/v1/organization-memberships/{id}` is a member of an organization; the organization is named in the query (`organization_id`). The same holds for invitations, role assignments, portal links and the other children listed below.

**The old paths.** `https://{environment}.cboxid.com/api/v1/…` keeps answering, with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers, until its callers have moved.

get.summary: List the published apps one person sees in one of their organizations, in catalog order. For an app's backend, with its own client-credentials token.
get.description:
Requires scope `app_catalog:resolve`. Danger: read.

What an app's backend asks to draw its app switcher for a person it has already signed
in — with the app's OWN client-credentials token (`grant_type=client_credentials`,
`scope=app_catalog:resolve`), so the switcher never needs the person's
`account:apps:read` grant, a reconnect or a sign-in hop. An administrator grants the
scope to the app in the console.

The items, their order and the envelope are exactly those of `GET /api/v1/me/apps` with
the same `organization_id`. A person who does not exist, is not active, or is not an
active member of the organization is the same `404 not_found`.

A hot read: no audit entry is written. Cache it for `meta.refresh_after` seconds, and
compare `meta.revision` to tell whether anything changed.

post.summary: Register an app
post.description:
Requires scope `apps:write`. Two ways to describe it:

- **From a blueprint** — send `GET /apps/{id}/blueprint`'s document from another
  environment as `blueprint` (promote staging to production). `name`,
  `redirect_uris` and `post_logout_redirect_uris` beside it replace the
  blueprint's own, since those usually name the environment it came from. A
  `private_key_jwt` blueprint needs `jwks`.
- **Short form** — `name` and `type` (`web`, `spa`, `cli`, `service`, `agent`; default
  `web`), which decide the client type, grants and default scopes as the console's
  "Create app" does. `advanced` takes `client_type` and `grant_types`.

The response carries `client_secret` for an app that authenticates with one —
**once**. Only its hash is kept, and an idempotent replay returns `client_secret: null`.

A platform scope reserved for the console (`vault.manage`, `decisions:read`) is
refused (`scope_not_grantable`), as is a registered API's scope this app's owner may
not hold. Danger: critical — it mints a credential.

post.summary: Invite someone to the organization
post.description:
Requires scope `invitations:write`. Mails a link; the person joins when they open it
and confirm. Inviting an address again replaces its earlier pending invitation.

- `role` — `admin` or `member` (default `member`). Never `owner`.
- `roles` — access roles granted when the invitation is accepted: role ids, or your
  app's manifest **keys** when `client_id` names the app that declared them. Only
  roles the organization's own administrators could grant are accepted: a **staff
  role** is refused (`422 role_not_assignable`) — grant it after they join, with
  `PUT …/members/{user_id}/roles/{role_id}`.
- `client_id` + `return_to` — after accepting, the person is sent to `return_to`,
  which must be on one of that app's registered redirect-URI origins (checked again
  when the invitation is accepted).
- `inviter_name` — who the mail says it is from. Defaults to the app's name, or the
  environment's.

Refusals: `409 already_member`, `409 access_role_conflict` (segregation of duties),
`422 unknown_role`, `422 role_not_assignable`, `422 unknown_app`,
`422 return_without_app`, `422 return_to_malformed`, `422 return_to_not_registered`,
`503 mail_failed` (nothing was created — retry).

post.summary: Add an existing user as a member
post.description:
Requires scope `members:write`. Straight in — no invitation, no mail. Name the user by
`user_id` or by `email`; they must exist in this environment (`422 user_not_found`).
A suspended or archived organization takes no new members (`409 organization_inactive`).

`roles` grants access roles at the same time — ids, or your app's manifest keys with
`client_id` — with the environment's authority (staff roles included). One the
organization cannot hold is `422 role_not_assignable`; a segregation-of-duties
conflict is `409 role_conflict`, and nothing is added.

`role` is `admin` or `member` (default `member`). `owner` is never assignable:
ownership moves with `transfer-ownership`.

**Idempotent for the same role**: repeating the request answers `200` with the
existing membership. A member on a *different* role is `409 already_member` — change
the role with `PATCH`.

post.summary: Lease a fresh access token for a person's connected account (Pipes)
post.description:
Returns a working access token for one person's connected account at a
third-party provider (GitHub, Google, Microsoft 365, Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot,
Linear, Notion), refreshing it first when it is about to expire. The app must be
granted the provider's pipe (Developers › Pipes); an app an organization owns may
only lease for that organization's members.

Whose token: a token issued to the app FOR a person leases that person's
connection, and `user_id` may only repeat it; a client-credentials token names the
person in `user_id`. The response is `Cache-Control: no-store`. Drop the token
when you are done and lease again next time.

parameters.description: The provider's key.
parameters.name: provider

user_id.description: The person, for a token not issued for one. With a person's token, may only name that person.

access_token.description: The provider's access token. Use it as a bearer token against the provider's API.

expires_at.description: When the PROVIDER stops accepting it. Null for tokens that do not expire.

lease_expires_at.description: When to drop it and lease again.

metadata.description: What the app needs to call the API at all — Salesforce's `instance_url`, Slack's `team.id`, Notion's `workspace_id`. Never a credential.

403.description:
Lease denied — the app is not granted this pipe, there is no such (enabled)
pipe, the person is not a member of the app's organization, or `user_id` names
someone other than the token's person. One response, with a constant message.

404.description: The app is granted the pipe, and the person has not connected the provider. Send them to `connect_url`.

409.description: The person must connect the provider again — it refused the refresh token, or the token expired with none. Send them to `connect_url`.

503.description: A needed refresh could not complete right now. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

get.summary: Read the environment-owner identity source
get.description:
Requires an environment key with `signals_source:read` and explicit operator
opt-in for this environment. Organization grants and delegated user tokens
cannot read this source. Records include pre-organization authentication.
The cursor follows committed sequence order and is bound to the source generation.
Follow `next_cursor`, including on empty pages; a stale generation or purged
cursor requires an explicit restart. Pages are at most 1000 records / 1 MiB.
Data follows the Signals 2.0.0 identity event contracts. Scope is attached by
the consumer's explicit grant; producer_environment is always host-bound.
Replay is limited to seven days, including raw-IP retention. A heartbeat
proves exporter maintenance, not complete coverage of every identity flow.

post.summary: Start a support session
post.description:
Requires scope `support:write`. A member of your staff (`actor_user_id`) signs in to
one of your apps (`client_id`) AS one of a customer's users (`user_id` in
`organization_id`), for a stated `reason`, for at most 60 minutes.

The actor must hold your app's own `support:impersonate` permission through an
**environment-wide** grant (see `PUT /users/{id}/environment-roles/{role_id}`);
otherwise `403 not_permitted`. The app must be a first-party app the environment
owns that uses the authorization-code grant (`422 client_not_eligible`). The target
must be an active member (`422 target_not_member`) of an active organization
(`409 organization_inactive`).

Send `redirect_uri` (registered for the app) and a PKCE S256 `code_challenge` to get
the first authorization `code` in the response. Your app redeems it at `/oauth/token`
with the verifier; every token carries `act: {"sub": actor_user_id}` and there is
never a refresh token. The session is audited on the customer's trail and the
environment's, and announced as the `support_session.started` webhook.

`scopes` in the response are exactly what every token of the session carries: the
ones asked for (or, with none, the app's registration), never `offline_access`, and
audienced the way the token endpoint audiences them — once any of them belongs to a
registered API, the token is for that API and a scope no API registered (such as
`apps.manifest`) is left out. Scopes of two registered APIs cannot be audienced to
one token and are refused before the session starts (`422 invalid_target`).

intents.description: What the link may set up.

sequence.description: The event's place in its organization's chain, from 1.

occurred_at.description: When it happened, as the sender said, to the millisecond.

schema_version.description: The version of its action's schema it was checked against; null when the action has none.

received_at.description: When it arrived. Retention counts from here.

prev_hash.description: The previous event's hash; 64 zeros for an organization's first.

events.description: The recorded events, in the order they were sent.

actor_metadata.description: A metadata schema (a subset of JSON Schema).

metadata.description: A metadata schema (a subset of JSON Schema).

organization_id.description: null for an export across the whole environment.

filters.description: The filters it was asked with.

Where the CSV downloads from once `ready` — signed, and valid for a few minutes;
read the export again for a fresh one. null otherwise, and on an idempotent replay.

type.description: The subject's type: `user`, or `group` for a userset.

relation.description: For a userset — everybody with this relation on the subject (`member` of `group:eng`). null for one subject.

tuple.description: The same tuple in the notation: `document:readme#viewer@group:eng#member`.

defined.description: false until a schema is first saved.

How the relation is decided, as a tree of one-key objects: `direct` (a list of
`{type, relation?}`), `computed` (a relation name), `from` (`{tupleset, relation}`),
`union` and `intersection` (lists of rewrites), `exclusion` (`{base, subtract}`).

UserPropertiesAccessToken.description: Issuer-audience OAuth access token with user_properties:read or user_properties:write and an explicit namespace grant. DPoP-bound tokens require the DPoP authorization scheme and proof header. An environment management API key is not accepted.

EnvironmentApiKey.description:
An environment API key, `cbid_env_…`. Created by the account that owns the environment,
in the console under Identity platform › Environment keys — not in the environment's own
console. Bound to that environment's host, and carries an explicit list of scopes; it may
also carry an expiry.

AppAccessToken.description:
An app's OWN OAuth access token from the client-credentials grant, issued by this
environment and standing for no person. Accepted only by the operations whose scope an
administrator may grant an app for this (`app_catalog:resolve`), and only when the token
carries it. DPoP-bound tokens require the DPoP authorization scheme and proof header.

ManagementAccessToken.description:
A PERSON's OAuth access token, issued by this environment's issuer and audienced to
its management plane (`resource=https://<environment-host>/mcp` — the same token the
MCP server takes). `cbox login` and MCP clients obtain one by signing the person in.

It may run an operation only when it carries the operation's scope AND the person
could run it on their own console here: an organization administrator, confined to
the organization the token is bound to. Operations that belong to the environment
console do not list it. Every critical operation answers `202 approval_required`
until the person approves it on their device.

On the organization's own roster (members, their roles, invitations, ownership, its
people's API keys) the organization's own rules hold, as on its People page: an
admin cannot change or remove an owner, nobody removes themselves, only the owner
transfers ownership, a staff-only role is `role_not_assignable`, and a customer
organization's roster — administered under Organization › Team — is `409 managed_elsewhere`. A DPoP-bound token is presented as
`Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a proof.

OrganizationAccessToken.description:
An organization member's OAuth access token from the PLATFORM ROOT, audienced to the
root's `/mcp` (`cbox login` at the root; an agent signed in there). Presented on the
ROOT's host, with `Cbox-Environment` naming the environment of the person's
organization to act in. It runs what that environment's console runs — when the
person's role administers environments and their membership reaches this one — and
only within the scopes it carries. Every critical operation answers
`202 approval_required` until the person approves it on their device. A DPoP-bound
token is presented as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a proof.

AppClientCredentials.description:
Your APP's own client credentials — `client_id:client_secret` as HTTP Basic
(`client_secret_basic`). `client_secret_post` and `private_key_jwt` are accepted
too, in the body, exactly as at the token endpoint.

VaultManagerToken.description:
An OAuth access token carrying the `vault.manage` scope. NOT an environment API
key: these routes are guarded by `scope:vault.manage`, which introspects an
access token, and a `cbid_env_` key introspects as inactive. Its `org` claim
selects the organization whose secrets it administers.

AgentToken.description:
An OAuth access token carrying the `vault.lease` scope. Its `org` claim selects
the organization whose secrets it may open — the vault's tenancy boundary.

AuthenticatorToken.description:
A DPoP-bound OAuth access token held by the Cbox ID authenticator app, obtained
via authorization_code + PKCE (S256) as a public client.

Because the token carries a `cnf.jkt`, every request must present it under the
`DPoP` auth scheme together with a matching proof — `htm`, `htu`, a fresh `jti`,
an `iat` within 60 seconds, and an `ath` equal to the SHA-256 of the token
itself. A plain `Bearer` presentation of a bound token is rejected.

AppsAppAccessToken.description: An access token issued by the current environment with the operation’s required scope and caller type. DPoP-bound tokens require their proof.

PersonToken.description: An access token you delegated, carrying `account:*` scopes. Management keys are refused.

OrganizationOrganizationAccessToken.description:
An organization member's access token from the platform root, audienced to the root's
`/mcp`. Bounded by the person's role in the organization and by its scopes. A DPoP-bound
token is presented as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a proof.

OrganizationApiKey.description: An organization key, `cbid_ws_…` — a role, optionally narrowed by scopes. Create and revoke keys in the console (Owner/Admin), or with `POST /workspace/keys`.

OperatorToken.description: An access token delegated by an active platform operator, carrying `operator:*` scopes. Management keys are refused.
